scores.name: 文字完整與按鈕尺寸

checks_against.candidate: The general 34px history-button rule could still override the mode-button width and reproduce the Chrome clipping.
checks_against.result: The later and more specific .m1-history .m1-mode-button selector overrides width with auto and enforces a 68px minimum.

checks_against.candidate: Chinese text could wrap or sit against the border even after increasing width.
checks_against.result: The dedicated rule adds 16px horizontal padding, white-space: nowrap, and a 12px Noto Sans TC font; both labels share the same class.

evidence.observation: Scene and 流程 use the same m1-mode-button class and retain their original click handlers.
evidence.effect: Both labels receive one symmetric sizing rule without changing mode-switch behavior.

evidence.observation: Icon buttons remain 34px, while mode buttons explicitly use width:auto, min-width:68px, padding:0 16px, and white-space:nowrap.
evidence.effect: The original clipping root cause is overridden locally, and the 68px size stays within the rubric's 64-88px range.

evidence.observation: Regression assertions require the exact sizing safeguards and reject a 34px mode-button width.
evidence.effect: Future changes cannot silently restore the reported narrow-button defect without failing tests.

problems: A live post-fix Chrome screenshot could not be captured because no Chrome control extension was connected; the score is capped below 95 rather than treating browser interaction as completed.

checks_against.candidate: The selected state might remain color-only or be unavailable to assistive technology.
checks_against.result: Each mode button binds aria-pressed directly to the same viewMode predicate that controls the visual active class.

checks_against.candidate: The new active style could recolor undo and redo controls.
checks_against.result: The active selector now requires both m1-mode-button and mode-active under m1-history, excluding icon controls.

evidence.observation: Scene and 流程 expose boolean aria-pressed states while preserving setViewMode('scene'/'flow') click actions.
evidence.effect: Visual and semantic state track the actual mode using the same source of truth.

evidence.observation: Inactive controls retain #e8e9e5 on #292a27; active mode controls use #20211f on #d9ff43 via a dedicated selector.
evidence.effect: Both states have clear light/dark contrast, and the active rule cannot target unrelated buttons.

evidence.observation: Tests require the dedicated class and aria-pressed binding for both modes.
evidence.effect: The accessibility state and style hook are protected against regression.

scores.name: 工具列空間與響應式穩定性

checks_against.candidate: Allocating more space could stretch the buttons excessively or displace adjacent controls.
checks_against.result: Buttons use width:auto with a 68px minimum rather than flex growth; the three-column 1fr/auto/1fr topbar grid and JSX control order are unchanged.

checks_against.candidate: The fix could alter existing narrow-window behavior.
checks_against.result: The 1050px rule still hides m1-history and changes the topbar to two columns; the 760px minimum-shell and secondary-action behavior are unchanged.

evidence.observation: The header remains grid-template-columns:1fr auto 1fr; mode controls have content-sized width and a 68px floor only.
evidence.effect: The central group receives enough room without being stretched to consume spare header space.

evidence.observation: The existing 1050px and 760px responsive rules remain present and unchanged in behavior.
evidence.effect: The local desktop fix does not replace the established responsive fallback strategy.

evidence.observation: Brand, undo, redo, Scene, 流程, autosave, and five file-action buttons remain in their prior order.
evidence.effect: No adjacent topbar capability was removed or reordered by the sizing repair.

problems: Direct live-Chrome viewport evidence is unavailable in this environment, so the score remains in the 90-94 band despite the bounded CSS and unchanged breakpoints.

checks_against.candidate: A visual-only CSS change might pass inspection while breaking the build or unrelated export behavior.
checks_against.result: The full suite passed TypeScript/build, PSD verification, all 40 tests, ESLint, and both performance benchmarks.

checks_against.candidate: Version metadata could be inconsistent across the app bundle and exported project manifest.
checks_against.result: package metadata, package lock, project-package toolVersion, cache-busted assets, and their tests all use 0.18.2.

evidence.observation: All required objective checks are recorded as passing; the restricted benchmark startup failure and successful authorized rerun are both disclosed.
evidence.effect: The delivery is supported by reproducible checks without hiding an environmental test-runner issue.

evidence.observation: New assertions cover both aria states, the dedicated selector, width override, minimum width, horizontal padding, nowrap, and rejection of 34px.
evidence.effect: The test suite directly covers the reported root cause and the acceptance constraints rather than only checking that CSS builds.

evidence.observation: Application and exported-package versions are both 0.18.2.
evidence.effect: The repair is ready for a traceable patch release.

summary: Round 1 internal audit finds the clipping root cause locally corrected and protected by direct regression assertions. Every criterion exceeds 90; live Chrome interaction was unavailable and is reflected as a score limitation rather than claimed evidence.
